newsitem.title: FRANCE: France Telecom has Italy ambitions.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom has Italy ambitions.

text.p: France Telecom said on Monday it had big ambitions for the Italian market and wanted to become the second-biggest operator there as part of its international expansion strategy.

But it had no comment on a newspaper report that it might be willing to take an equity stake in loss-making information technology group Olivetti, as suggested by the International Herald Tribune newspaper.
"Concerning the capital of Olivetti we have no comment to make. We will follow with interest any developments in Olivetti's capital," a France Telecom spokesman said.
Financial analysts said France Telecom could not become too involved in Olivetti as it could endanger its partial privatisation due for spring 1997.

"France Telecom will want to show to its future shareholders that it has a tight and conservative strategy concerning international expansion and that its first priority is to reduce its debt," said Ian Macleod of Natwest Sellier in Paris.
"To go into Olivetti at the moment, even though the shares are cheap, would be risky and very strange indeed," he added.
But analysts noted that France Telecom would in the long run want to have a stable relationship with Olivetti as an industrial ally in breaking open the Italian market.

Any restructuring of Olivetti's capital would be studied with interest in Paris because the, now, state-owned French group would not want to see a rival getting on board nor would it like to see the door being shut on any future share stake.
Analysts said that if France Telecom participated in a restructuring of Olivetti by taking a five percent stake, this would not be beyond the realm of possibilities.
The France Telecom spokesman said his company "had been in talks for many months" with Olivetti concerning their joint interest in Infostrada.
"We have said in the past that we aim to become the second biggest operator in Italy," he added.
In August, France Telecom and Olivetti signed a draft agreement to buy a 70 percent stake in the Italian state railways' (FS) domestic telecom network.
In these talks, France Telecom is also representing its other strategic partners Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp.

In November, Olivetti launched its Infostrada joint venture with Bell Atlantic of the United States in which they, France Telecom, Sprint and Deutsche Telecom aim to rival state-controlled Telecom Italia Spa.
The venture will spend 200 billion lire ($131 million) in 1996 and 1997 to set up a network by 1998, when the market will be liberalised.
Olivetti is also 41.3 percent owner of Omnitel, the second biggest mobile telephone operator in Italy behind Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM). France Telecom runs French market-leader Itineris.

France Telecom has a two-pronged approach to the 1998 European market liberalisation. On the one hand it is arming itself to do battle in France with domestic rivals such as Cie Generale des Eaux Cegetel and foreign groups such as British Telecom Plc and AT&T.
But on the other hand it is actively entering other markets to rival exisiting monopolies and it has also an increasing presence in Belgium. ($1=1524 Lire)
